summary.title: Eigenface using OpenCV (C++/Python)
summary.one_liner: You learn how EigenFaces apply PCA to aligned face images and how to compute, reshape and blend them into new faces with OpenCV in C++ and Python.
takeaways: EigenFaces are principal components of a dataset of aligned face images, and a new face is the mean face plus weighted EigenFaces.
Each image is flattened into one long row vector (e.g. 100x100x3 gives 30k elements) to form a data matrix for PCA.
OpenCV's PCA class (C++) or cv2.PCACompute (Python) returns the mean and eigenvectors; eigenvectors are reshaped back into images.
Slider weights are shifted by MAX_SLIDER_VALUE/2 so that negative weights can be applied to create new faces.
summary.summary: The post explains EigenFaces as an application of PCA to human face images, first recapping PCA and how an image becomes a high-dimensional vector. It walks through the steps: gathering about 200 aligned CelebA images, building a data matrix with one image per row, computing principal components with OpenCV, and reshaping eigenvectors into EigenFaces. It then presents C++ and Python code (credited to Subham Rajgaria) that shows the mean face and lets users blend 10 EigenFaces with trackbar sliders to generate new faces.
